The exclusive two-hour rail excursion provided a firsthand look at MSE’s investments and its role in driving job creation and sustaining the broader Mississippi Gulf Coast economy. The event drew prominent national and state leadership, including Federal Railroad Administrator David Fink, U.S. Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R.-Miss.), and U.S. Rep. Michael Ezell (R-Miss.). They were joined on the tour by Nicole James, Canadian National’s Southern Region vice president, as well as officials from the Port of Pascagoula, Jackson and George County government, state legislators, and regional economic development partners. candidates.title: EBT Foundation exercises right to purchase Mount Union trackage
candidates.excerpt: MOUNT UNION, Pa. — The East Broad Top Foundation has exercised its right of first refusal to buy a 4.7-mile segment of East Broad Top main line, as well as the railroad’s dual-gauge yard in Mount Union. The foundation on Wednesday, Oct. 7, met its deadline to inform the seller, a nonprofit organization led by DuBois, Pa., businessman Larry Salone, that it would exercise the right to purchase the main line and yard. Judge Ray A. Ghaner had previously ruled that the right of first refusal remained valid [see “Judge rules that East Broad Top Foundation can buy …,” Trains.com, Oct. 1, 2026]. Salone and entrepreneur Stephen D. Lane, who had offered $2 million for the trackage with the intention of launching a short line, argued it had expired. The EBT Foundation matched that $2 million offer earlier, citing the first-refusal right. candidates.title: An interview with Jack Huygens of ‘Rolling Line’ model railroad simulator
candidates.excerpt: Nearly 10 years after its 2018 release, Rolling Line is still going strong! As an independent PC and VR sandbox game, it simulates model railroading that attracts hobbyists who may not have the time or space to build a real-life layout, as well as those who are planning to build one. Developer and owner of Gaugepunk Games, Jack Huygens joined Trains.com’s Lucas Iverson to discuss more. Watch the extended video interview with Jack Huygens of Rolling Line on Trains.com Video. Q: For those who may not be familiar with it, how would you summarize Rolling Line? A: It’s a virtual model railway game. I’ve seen a lot of software out there that’s very technical, and it’s all about planning a railway. Rolling Line is not going for that angle. candidates.title: AAR Reports Weekly Rail Traffic for the Week Ending October 3, 2026
candidates.excerpt: The Association of American Railroads (AAR) reported U.S. rail traffic for the week ending October 3, 2026. For this week, total U.S. weekly rail traffic was 529,712 carloads and intermodal units, up 5.1 percent compared with the same week last year. Total carloads for the week ending October 3 were 230,711 carloads, up 2.4 percent compared with the same week in 2025, while U.S. weekly intermodal volume was 299,001 containers and trailers, up 7.4 percent compared to 2025. Seven of the 10 carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They included metallic ores and metals, up 2,647 carloads, to 23,387; coal, up 1,627 carloads, to 58,163; and petroleum and petroleum products, up 1,286 carloads, to 11,804. Commodity groups that posted decreases compared with the same week in 2025 were grain, down 1,160 carloads, to 21,170; farm products excl. grain, and food, down 720 carloads, to 16,935; and chemicals, down 49 carloads, to 32,891. candidates.title: Rosatom folds Delo into expanding logistics platform
candidates.excerpt: Rosatom folds Delo into expanding logistics platform Russia’s state-owned Rosatom has completed the buyout of Delo Group founder Sergei Shishkarev’s controlling stake, taking full control of one of the country’s largest transport and container logistics groups. Rosatom, which previously held 49% of Delo, has acquired Shishkarev’s remaining 51% and will now begin consolidating the company with its other transport holdings, including shipping and logistics group FESCO. Neither side disclosed the final consideration. The “Russian roulette” buyout mechanism triggered earlier this year valued Shishkarev’s 51% holding at RUB77bn ($900m), while Rosatom’s 49% stake had been priced at RUB74bn. Rosatom chief Alexei Likhachev said the group will establish a common management centre for Delo, FESCO and its other transport assets, bringing together shipping, ports, rail, road transport and forwarding. candidates.title: Tanker attack off Qatar widens Gulf shipping conflict
candidates.excerpt: The war on merchant shipping in the Middle East has taken a worrying geographical turn, with casualties reported aboard a tanker attacked off Qatar, hundreds of miles west of the Strait of Hormuz, while a containership has also come under fire in the Red Sea. The Antigua and Barbuda-flagged oil/chemical tanker Acers (IMO: 9301902) was struck by multiple projectiles on Wednesday evening, approximately 51 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, according to maritime security firm Vanguard. UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) confirmed the attack at around 1900 UTC, reporting casualties but providing no details on their number or severity. Most attacks since Iranian strikes on commercial shipping resumed on September 28 have been concentrated around the Strait of Hormuz. Wednesday’s incident, deep inside the Arabian Gulf, marks the first reported attack outside the strait during the latest escalation. candidates.title: Savannah achieves record container volumes in September
candidates.excerpt: Savannah achieves record container volumes in September The Port of Savannah achieved a record September for container volumes, moving 504,015 twenty-foot equivalent container units last month, an increase of 3.7 percent compared to September 2025. Georgia Ports’ September performance brings the first quarter of its fiscal year to more than 1.5 million TEUs, up 40,560 TEUs or 2.7 percent. The quarter represents the second-best quarter in the company’s history (trailing only fiscal year 2023 Q1). Appalachian Regional Port volumes were up 13% for the first quarter of the fiscal year compared to the same period last year. Strong consumer spending and an extended peak season supported GPA’s September trade growth. Peak volumes were pushed into September because of typhoon-related delays at Asian ports. candidates.title: ASIC halts offers in three more private credit funds
candidates.excerpt: ASIC halts offers in three more private credit funds Australia’s corporate regulator has halted offers in three more private credit funds managed by Australian Secure Capital Fund (ASCF), as troubles mount in the sector. The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) said in a statement that it had made an interim stop order on the product disclosure statement (PDS) for the ASCF Premium Capital Fund, ASCF Select Income Fund and ASCF High Yield Fund. The order prevents ASCF from offering, issuing, selling or transferring interests in the funds. ASIC said it was concerned that the PDS failed to disclose information about the funds’ loan portfolio and diversification metrics, and that the information it did disclose was not presented clearly. The regulator said the PDS may also contain a “misleading and deceptive “statement and omit information about the cost of disposing of an interest in the funds.
